Project-specific C++ compilation contract (repeat verbatim here): use the exact collision-query signature bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const (or omit that helper entirely); no function may refer to a grow variable that is absent from its parameters or local declarations

Project-specific C++ compilation contract (repeat verbatim here): specify an exact Game constructor initializer containing snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3); constructor-body assignment is forbidden, and dimensions must be validated before any game tick
CMake rule: each target_compile_options flag must be a separate list argument, never one quoted string containing multiple flags
Domain Reasoning: Entities: Board (grid dimensions and walls), Snake (body as deque of Positions, current Direction, growth), Food (single Position), Game (orchestrates ticks, score, reset, RNG boundary).

State transitions: On each tick, compute next head Position from Direction; validate within Board; detect self-collision using body occupancy logic; optionally grow when consuming Food; update score; place new Food via RNG.
Direction rules: Reject immediate reversal (e.g., cannot go Left if moving Right). Queue and apply direction changes safely before movement.
Random boundary: Use IRandom interface with DefaultRandom implementation; seedable and deterministic for tests; no OS or time dependencies in tests.
Collision detection: Check wall collision against Board bounds; check self-collision against Snake body with the rule that moving into the tail is allowed only if not growing.
Food placement: Use RNG to select unoccupied cells; handle full-board case (snake fills board) deterministically and finish game (win or no more food).
Game lifecycle: Start centered; initial length 3; initial Direction Right; provide reset that restores initial state; expose score and game-over status.

API contracts and includes (reiterated): include/IRandom.h must directly include <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random>; include/Game.h must directly include "Board.h", "IRandom.h", "Snake.h", "Types.h", <cstddef>, <deque>, and <optional>; include/Types.h is the sole definition site for Position and Direction; use exact signature bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const; Game constructor initializer must contain snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3).
Domain Expectations: Grid-based movement: the snake advances one cell per tick in its current Direction.
Immediate reversal prevention: direction updates that would reverse into the neck are ignored.
Food consumption: when head reaches Food, score increments and snake grows by one segment in that tick.
Random food placement on an unoccupied cell using IRandom; deterministic under seeded DefaultRandom.
Wall collision ends the game; Board bounds are inclusive of [0,width) x [0,height).
Self-collision ends the game; moving into the tail is allowed only if not growing that tick.
Game exposes reset(), tick(), setDirection(Direction), isGameOver(), getScore(), getSnake(), getFood().
Construction validates dimensions; Game constructs Snake in the initializer list with snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3).
Product Goals: Deliver a clean, testable core Snake game with deterministic behavior.
Preserve strict protocol and compilation contracts for seamless automated evaluation.
Keep modules small, self-contained, and easy to extend.
User Stories: As a player, I want the snake to move on a grid and respond to direction input, without allowing immediate reversal.
As a player, I want to eat food to grow the snake and increase my score.
As a player, I want the game to end when I hit a wall or my own body, and be able to reset.
As a developer, I want deterministic tests with a seeded RNG to verify core rules without real-time or UI dependencies.
Competitive Analysis: Console-based snake implementations: minimal UI, often entangled logic and I/O.
SFML-based C++ snake tutorials: richer visuals but typically weak separation and poor testability.
Browser JavaScript snake clones: easy to run, but rarely deterministic for unit tests.
Katas for snake rules: emphasize logic correctness, but often lack clear module boundaries and build/test protocol adherence.

Requirement Analysis: We must produce a C++17 repository architecture for a Snake game using CMake with exact protocol files: CMakeLists.txt, src/Main.cpp, tests/test_main.cpp. There must be exactly one test file. The design separates pure domain logic (Board, Snake, Game, Types) from boundaries (IRandom/DefaultRandom). Deterministic tests rely on a seeded RNG. Strict compilation contracts must be upheld: include/Types.h is the sole definition site for Position and Direction, and any header that mentions either must include "Types.h" directly. include/IRandom.h declares both IRandom and DefaultRandom; src/Random.cpp must include "IRandom.h" exactly and must never include or refer to a nonexistent Random.h. include/IRandom.h must directly include <cstddef>, <cstdint>, and <random>; size types are std::size_t and seed types are std::uint32_t because std::mt19937 is a declared member. include/Game.h must directly include "Board.h", "IRandom.h", "Snake.h", "Types.h", <cstddef>, <deque>, and <optional>; forward declarations and transitive includes are forbidden for these dependencies. If we implement a helper for self-collision, it must use exactly: bool wouldSelfCollide(const Position& next, bool grow) const; no function may refer to a grow variable not present in its parameters or locals. Game must validate dimensions before ticks and must construct its Snake in the constructor initializer list with exactly: snake_(Position{static_cast<int>(width / 2), static_cast<int>(height / 2)}, Direction::Right, 3); no constructor-body assignment. CMake compile options must list each flag as a separate argument, not a quoted multi-flag string. The runtime entry provides a small, non-interactive demonstration and exits.
